label: May 1916
headline: Strike from the Trentino
deck: An Austrian offensive from the mountains threatens the Italian plain
caption: Austro-Hungarian mountain troops haul a gun up a snow-filled gully
body: On 15 May Austro-Hungarian armies attack out of the Trentino, from the mountains above the plain of Venetia. Field Marshal Conrad means to punish Italy for changing sides: a thrust to the plain would cut off the Italian armies on the Isonzo.

After a crushing bombardment the attackers take Arsiero and Asiago on their plateau. Then supply over the mountain roads falters, General Cadorna brings up a new army by rail, and the advance is checked on the last ridges before the plain.
At Verdun French troops under General Mangin break into Fort Douaumont on 22 May and hold part of it for two days before they are thrown out again with heavy loss.
In Mesopotamia the prisoners of Kut, British and Indian, begin a long march north into captivity; many will not survive it.
briefs: The leaders of the Easter Rising are executed in Dublin
Britain extends conscription to married men
Germany and Britain set their clocks an hour ahead to save daylight
